text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The government's 1997 budget proposals will allocate 365 billion escudos to the social security system, a government source told the paper.
- The government will not provide compensation to loss-making port company Casa do Douro.
- South Korean industrial group Hyundai does not plan to invest in a factory in Portugal despite the efforts of Economy Minister Augusto Mateus.
- Pulp company Portucel Industrial will return to the capital market for a 15 billion escudos loan, said Banco Santander de Negocios Portugal, leader of the banking syndicate.

- Portugal's railway company Caminhos de Ferro Portugueses (CP) has opened a public competition for the electrification of 350 km of railway lines in the Alentejo and Algarve in southern Portugal. The investment is estimated to cost up to 20 billion escudos and involves work that should last until the year 2002.
- Top military officers met President Jorge Sampaio on Monday and expressed concerns over budget cuts for 1997.

- The builders' association has presented a plan to boost the construction sector and cut rents. The building of new residential housing with state financial support could create 100,000 jobs within 5 years, according to the proposal. The Socialist government is divided over the proposal and has not yet made a formal response.
